title: [Segfault Bug] Out-of-bounds write of at::native::cpubla::gemm (bfloat16) in at::native::cpu_flash_attention_backward

labels.name: module: crash
labels.description: Problem manifests as a hard crash, as opposed to a RuntimeError

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

In PyTorch’s CPU implementation of [cpu_flash_attention_backward](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/FlashAttentionKernel.cpp#L745), the [cpublas::gemm](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/CPUBlas.cpp#L329) performs out-of-bounds memory writes when it's dispatched to **openblas sbgemm_** routine. 

This results causes **nondeterministic crashes** and **memory corruption**. The fault is observed in: `aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/FlashAttentionKernel.cpp::cpu_flash_attention_backward`. 

this bug can be reproduced using pytorch unit tests of `TestSDPACpuOnlyCPU.test_scaled_dot_product_fused_attention`

```bash
for i in {1..1000}
do
python test/test_transformers.py TestSDPACpuOnlyCPU.test_scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_mask_vs_math_cpu_fused_kernel0_bfloat16_batch_size_12_q_seq_len_1030_kv_seq_len_17_n_head_3_head_dim_8_mask_dim_2_bool_mask_False_train_True_casual_False_set_attn_mask_False_cpu_bfloat16
done
```

#### Root cause and Correction of cpublas::gemm

This segfault bug is caused by incorrect behavior of [bf16 cpublas::gemm](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/CPUBlas.cpp#L356-L373), which mishandles strided output matrices.

Specifically, it:

1. Allocates a temporary FP32 buffer of size ldc * n
2. Copies and converts the full ldc * n region from the output matrix C (BF16 → FP32)
3. Performs sbgemm over the logical m × n region using the passed ldc
4. Converts the entire ldc * n result back to BF16 and writes it back to C

This logic assumes C is contiguous or has exclusive access to ldc * n elements, which is not valid when C is a view into a larger tensor (as in multi-head attention). As a result, it overwrites memory outside the m × n region, corrupting adjacent data.

**Expected behavior:**
cpublas::gemm should only copy, compute, and write back the m × n region as described by the passed dimensions and ldc stride, not the full ldc × n span.

### Error Explanation of flash attention:

The bug occurs in [`cpu_flash_attention_backward`](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/FlashAttentionKernel.cpp#L745), where `cpublas::gemm` is called on `grad_q`, `grad_k`, and `grad_v` which are of strided views.

Take `grad_q` as an example. Its shape is: `[batchSize, qSize, numHeads, headSize]`. Each attention head is processed as a logical matrix: `[qSize, headSize]`.  But in memory, **each row is spaced by `numHeads * headSize` elements**, not just `headSize`. That is: `ldc = numHeads * headSize > m = headSize`. 

This layout is safe for the first head (`head == 0`), where writes begin at the start of the grad tensor. However, for **`head > 0`**, the output pointer `C` starts at an offset in the middle of the tensor. Since `cpublas::gemm` writes back a full `ldc * n` region from that offset, it overruns the intended slice and **corrupts memory belonging to other heads or unrelated data**.

| Head Index | Behavior               |
|------------|------------------------|
| ✅ `head == 0` | Writes start at beginning — overflow is hidden |
| ❌ `head > 0`  | Writes past intended slice — causes memory corruption |


### Proposed fixup:

code in this https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/aten/src/ATen/native/CPUBlas.cpp#L356-L373 should be changed to 

```
   if (use_blas_gemm(transa, transb, m, n, k, lda, ldb, ldc)) {
      int m_ = m, n_ = n, k_ = k, lda_ = lda, ldb_ = ldb, ldc_ = ldc;
      char transa_ = to_blas(transa), transb_ = to_blas(transb);
      float alpha_ = alpha, beta_ = beta;
      int c_size = n_ * m_;
      // C matrix in OpenBLAS sbgemm are of type "float" so we have to convert, copy and copy back.
      at::BFloat16 * c_ptr = c; 
      std::vector<float> float_v(c_size, 0.0f);
      for (const auto j : c10::irange(n)) {
        for (const auto i : c10::irange(m)) {
          float_v[j * m + i] = c10::convert<float>(*(c_ptr + i));
        }
        c_ptr += ldc_;
      }
      sbgemm_(&transa_, &transb_,
              &m_, &n_, &k_,
              &alpha_,
              a, &lda_,
              b, &ldb_,
              &beta_,
              float_v.data(), &m_);
      c_ptr = c;
      for (const auto j : c10::irange(n)) {
        for (const auto i : c10::irange(m)) {
          *(c_ptr + i) = c10::convert<at::BFloat16>(float_v[j * m + i]);
        }
        c_ptr += ldc_;
      }
      return;
   }
```
